items.title: Vigilo – Local audit trail and cost tracker for AI coding agents
items.raw_excerpt: I realized I'd spent $197 in a single day using Claude Code and Cursor without any visibility into what they were actually doing. No breakdown of which operations cost what, no record of what files were read or written, no way to audit what the agent executed on my behalf. So I built vigilo. It sits between your AI agent and your system as an MCP server, logging every tool call — file reads, writes, shell commands, git operations — to a local append-only JSONL ledger. For write operations it captures a unified diff. Every event gets a risk level (read/write/exec), timing, git context, model, and token count. Nothing leaves your machine. No accounts, no telemetry, no cloud. Arguments and results can be encrypted at rest with AES-256-GCM — the key never leaves ~/.vigilo/. Works with Claude C

items.title: OpenTangl – Autonomous AI dev engine for multi-repo products
items.raw_excerpt: OpenTangl is an open-source TypeScript tool that runs an autonomous development loop. You define a product vision and point it at one or more repos. It proposes tasks, writes code via GPT-4o or Claude, verifies builds, creates PRs, reviews diffs, and merges — in a closed loop. The part I found most useful: it manages cross-repo dependencies. If a UI feature needs a new API endpoint, it builds and merges the API task first, then builds the frontend. Task ordering via `depends_on` fields. It runs locally on your machine. No cloud services, no accounts beyond an LLM API key and GitHub CLI. A cycle of 4-5 tasks costs about $0.30-0.50 in API calls. Built this for my own projects over the past few months. Open-sourced it today. TypeScript, ~17k lines, MIT licensed.

items.title: AgentKeeper – Cross-model memory for AI agents
items.raw_excerpt: I built AgentKeeper to solve a problem I kept hitting: every time I switched LLM providers or an agent crashed, it lost all context. AgentKeeper introduces a Cognitive Reconstruction Engine (CRE) that stores agent memory independently of any provider and reconstructs optimal context when switching models. Benchmark: 19/20 critical facts recovered when switching GPT-4 → Claude (and reverse). Bidirectional, tested on real API calls. Supports OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Ollama. SQLite persistence. MIT license.

For a considerable period, progress in medical AI primarily revolved around the acquisition and reasoning of medical knowledge, with models' "intelligence" often measured by static benchmarks such as medical exam questions and clinical Q&A datasets. Under this evaluation framework, models were considered to possess high medical capability as long as they provided correct answers under conditions of complete information and closed questions. With the rise of large language models, this approach quickly achieved breakthroughs, with multiple systems reaching or surpassing human expert levels in tests like MedQA, leading to optimistic industry assessments about whether "medical AI has matured." However, as these models were gradually introduced into interactive scenarios closer to real clinical practice, a long-overlooked issue emerged: real medical practice is not about making diagnoses based on complete information but a dynamic process of gradually approaching decisions through continuous questioning, risk identification, and information integration under conditions of high uncertainty. The 2026 CCTV Spring Festival Gala reached a historic high in "tech content," with collective pushes from three major sectors: AI, robotics, and consumer electronics. Frequent appearances were made not only by Volcano Engine, Doubao, Bilibili, and Xiaohongshu, but also by deep involvement from embodied intelligence companies like Magic Atom, Songyan Power, Galaxy General, and Yushu. Securing a spot on the Spring Festival Gala partnership list is no easy task. The appearance of MOVA TPEAK not only breaks the long-standing dominance of traditional consumer goods like alcohol and milk on the Spring Festival Gala stage but also marks Chinese smart hardware brands entering a new phase.

excerpt_i18n.en:
Author: Wu You  Editor: Yu Kuai  
If evaluating the market acceptance of an AI hardware product by its crowdfunding amount, one million dollars is a threshold. Surpassing this figure indicates that product-market fit is essentially viable, signaling the birth of another hit product.  

The AI card phone MindOne, which garnered significant attention at CES 2026, was launched on Kickstarter in July last year. Priced starting at $299, it attracted support from 3,411 backers worldwide. Within 30 days of its release, it raised approximately $1.48 million. Supporters expressed interest in its portability, AI features, and retro design.  

MindOne’s card-style design is compact and lightweight, with a thickness of 8.9mm and a weight of 136g, appealing to many users who pursue a minimalist lifestyle. Its 50-megapixel Sony main camera, along with a 180-degree reversible camera design, is also regarded as a highlight.  

In terms of AI functionality, the device features dual-system switching between Android 15 and iKKO AI OS. Users can switch to AI OS focus mode with one click, enabling offline AI functions such as real-time translation, speech-to-text, and image analysis to enhance efficiency.  

For expandability, the detachable keyboard case harks back to the "BlackBerry" era, receiving widespread acclaim from tech enthusiasts and retro aficionados.  

Just last week, iKKO completed its domestic debut at the INNO100 offline experience store in Shenzhen, accelerating its expansion into the Chinese market ahead of the Spring Festival.  

"Our primary target markets are Europe, the United States, Japan, and Southeast Asia, with user groups covering white-collar professionals."

Superar esa cifra indica que el Product-Market Fit es básicamente viable y que ha nacido otro producto exitoso. El teléfono de tarjeta de IA MindOne, muy destacado en el CES 2026, se lanzó en julio del año pasado en la plataforma de crowdfunding Kickstarter. Con un precio inicial de 299 dólares, atrajo el apoyo de 3,411 patrocinadores globales. En 30 días, recaudó aproximadamente 1.48 millones de dólares. Los patrocinadores expresaron interés por su portabilidad, funciones de IA y diseño retro. El diseño de tarjeta de MindOne es compacto y ligero, con un grosor de 8 mm.

excerpt_i18n.en:
Author: Wu You  Editor: Yu Kuai  
Shortly after the 2023 Spring Festival holiday ended, employees at Teeni.AI received a company-wide notice from CEO Yuan Lin: "All business shifts to AI, focusing fully on youth-oriented intelligent agents." This decision stemmed from an intuition born of her dual identity—she is both a serial entrepreneur deeply involved in the children’s hardware sector and a mother of two children born in the 2010s.  

A decade ago, during her first entrepreneurial venture, Yuan Lin’s product, Pudding Doudou, belonged to the AI 1.0 era. The team initially developed an OS system before targeting the children’s market, but the AI technology at the time "could only fool kids." The most popular feature was using the robot as a "messenger," bridging communication between parents and children, which formed her initial understanding of children’s needs.  

Her second venture, Listening Bear, originally focused on English learning scenarios. It wasn’t until the explosion of GPT technology, as she watched her own children skillfully using AI to search for information and ask questions, that Yuan Lin suddenly realized: "This wave of opportunity cannot be missed." She immediately halted the original plans, led the training of a dedicated large model for youth, and launched an AI portable intelligent agent.  

Her experience of chatting with thousands of children each year helped her grasp the core of interacting with the post-2010 generation: "You have to squat down and speak their language; respect is more important than anything." She pointedly criticized a common industry flaw—many AI companion hardware products rely on generic models with forced personas. In her view, AI should not play an omnipotent role but should serve as a "cognitive bridge," helping children connect the virtual and physical worlds.

excerpt_i18n.es: Autor: Wu You. Editor: Yu Kuai. Justo después de las vacaciones del Año Nuevo chino de 2023, los empleados de Teeni.AI recibieron una notificación de su CEO, Yuan Lin: "Todas las operaciones se orientarán hacia la IA, centrándonos al máximo en los agentes inteligentes para adolescentes." Detrás de esta decisión hay una intuición derivada de su doble identidad: es tanto una emprendedora en serie con profunda experiencia en el sector de hardware infantil como madre de dos hijos nacidos después de 2010. En su primer emprendimiento hace diez años, su producto Pudding Doudou aún estaba en la era de la IA 1.0. El equipo primero desarrolló un sistema operativo y luego se enfocó en el sector infantil, pero la tecnología de IA de entonces "solo podía engañar a los niños". La función más popular era hacer que el robot actuara como "mensajero".
